contests.title: Allamuchy Township School District — school improvement bonds

provenance.sourceOrg: Warren County Clerk — current2026 General Election public-question documents
provenance.quote: The Board of Education of the Township of Allamuchy in the County of Warren, New Jersey (the “Board”) is authorized to: (a) undertake various improvements, renovations, and upgrades at Allamuchy Township School, including but not limited to the replacement of roofing, windows, and wood siding, masonry repairs, and mechanical and HVAC system upgrades, including acquisition of any fixtures, equipment, and site work; (b) undertake various improvements, renovations, and upgrades at Mountain Villa School, including but not limited to repairs and upgrades to windows and lintels, masonry repairs, and upgrades to the insulation, including acquisition of any fixtures, equipment and site work; (c) appropriate $16,421,600 for such improvements; and (d) issue bonds in an amount not to exceed $16,421,600. The final eligible costs for the projects approved by the New Jersey Commissioner of Education are $16,421,600 (consisting of $15,746,600 for Allamuchy Township School and $675,000 for Mountain Villa School). The projects include $0 for school facility construction elements in addition to the facilities efficiency standards developed by the Commissioner of Education or not otherwise eligible for State of New Jersey (the “State”) support pursuant to N.J.S.A. 18A:7G-5(g). The State debt service aid percentage is equal to 40% of the annual debt service due with respect to the final eligible costs of the projects. The Board of Education is authorized to transfer funds among the projects approved at this election.

measures.questionText: Shall the County of Warren amend the Warren County Open Space, Farmland, Floodplain, and Historic Preservation Trust Fund to include the purpose of stewardship of permanently preserved lands acquired for recreation and conservation purposes that are designed to restore or enhance its utilization for those purposes and allow the use of previously collected funds for those purposes?
measures.officialStatement: A "YES" vote will permit the County of Warren to include natural resource management, habitat restoration, and stewardship as eligible activities on permanently preserved land acquired for recreation and conservation purposes. These include projects that are designed to enhance or restore the land's utilization for those purposes as eligible activities funded as part of the Warren County Open Space, Farmland, Floodplain Protection and Historic Preservation Trust Fund. A "YES" vote will not increase taxes. A “NO” vote is that you do not approve this amendment to the Open Space Trust Fund.

measures.questionText: Should the prohibition of data centers anywhere within the Town of Belvidere be pursued as part of the re- examination of the Town’s Master Plan?
measures.officialStatement: The development of a data center within the Town has the potential to generate significant tax revenue. At the same time, concern has been raised with respect to data centers utilizing excessive amounts of water and electricity as well as generating excessive noise from roof-mounted HVAC units. At present, data centers are not a permitted use in any zone within the Town. However, data centers are not an expressly prohibited use, and a data center developer could make application for variance relief. A YES vote would mean that you are in favor of expressly prohibiting data centers as an allowable use within the Town that would completely prohibit the ability of a data center to be built within the Town and eliminate any potential tax revenue from such a development. A NO vote would mean that you are not in favor of expressly prohibiting data centers and are in favor of retaining the ability of the Town’s Planning Board or Board of Adjustment and its professionals to consider a future application for a data center and potentially approve the application, with appropriate conditions.

The program shall provide for annual contributions to a deferred income account for each active volunteer member that meets the eligibility criteria and in accordance with the schedule adopted by the Township of Mansfield; (a) For regular annual services: a minimum of $100.00 and a maximum of $1,150.00 per year.
measures.officialStatement: The Township of Mansfield has decided to create a Length of Service Awards Program (LOSAP) for members of the volunteer fire departments that serve the citizens of the Township of Mansfield. The general requirements for a LOSAP are as set forth in State law (N.J.S.A. 40A:14-183, et seq.) Each volunteer fire fighter that performs the amount of service required by the Ordinance will have a minimum of $100.00 to a maximum of $1,150.00 per year deposited into a tax deferred income account that will earn interest for the volunteer. The cost will be budgeted annually in the budget of the Township of Mansfield and is anticipated to be $70,000.00 per year. Additional details on the program may be found in the Ordinance adopted by the Township of Mansfield, which is available for public inspection, along with a copy of the State enabling law in the Township Clerk's Office, located in the Municipal Building, 100 Port Murray Road, Port Murray, New Jersey between 9:00am and 4:00pm, Mondays through Fridays, holidays and weekends excepted.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adds natural-resource management, habitat restoration and stewardship of permanently preserved recreation and conservation land to the allowed uses of Warren County’s Open Space, Farmland, Floodplain and Historic Preservation Trust Fund. Projects must restore or enhance the land’s use for recreation or conservation; previously collected money could be used for these purposes. The official statement says approval would not increase taxes.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the expanded stewardship uses, including use of previously collected funds.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this amendment to the trust fund’s permitted uses.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes the Allamuchy school board to spend $16,421,600 and issue up to that amount in bonds for improvements at Allamuchy Township School and Mountain Villa School, with equipment, fixtures and site work. Allamuchy work includes replacing roofing, windows and wood siding, masonry repairs, and mechanical, heating, ventilation and air-conditioning upgrades. Mountain Villa work includes window and lintel repairs and upgrades, masonry repairs and insulation upgrades. All $16,421,600 is approved as eligible costs: $15,746,600 for Allamuchy and $675,000 for Mountain Villa. The stated state-aid calculation is 40% of annual debt payments associated with those eligible costs; the board could transfer funds among projects approved at this election.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve these school projects and up to $16,421,600 in bonds.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this project and bond authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Asks whether Belvidere should pursue an explicit townwide prohibition on data centers during its Master Plan review. Data centers currently are not permitted in any town zone, but are not expressly prohibited; a developer could seek a variance, according to the official explanation. The referendum is nonbinding.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Express support for pursuing an explicit townwide data-center prohibition as part of the Master Plan review.
measureRecords.noMeans: Express opposition to that prohibition and support retaining the opportunity for town planning officials to review a future application and potentially approve it with conditions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Establishes a Length of Service Awards Program for active volunteer firefighters serving Mansfield who meet the ordinance’s service and eligibility requirements and township contribution schedule. Each qualifying volunteer would receive an annual deposit of at least $100 and at most $1,150 into an interest-earning, tax-deferred income account. The township would budget for the program each year, with an anticipated annual cost of $70,000.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve establishing the proposed firefighter service-award program with these contribution limits and requirements.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject establishing this proposed service-award program.
